new_entities.name: Creatine monohydrate supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral creatine monohydrate supplementation used to support training adaptations and high-intensity exercise performance.

new_entities.name: Muscle mass gains during resistance training
new_entities.description: Longitudinal increases in lean mass or hypertrophy during a structured resistance-training program.

edges.effect_quant: Meta-analyses suggest creatine adds roughly 1.1 to 1.4 kg of lean or fat-free mass beyond resistance training alone, with smaller direct-imaging hypertrophy effects.
edges.population: healthy adults doing progressive resistance training
edges.mechanism: Creatine can improve training volume and phosphocreatine recovery, potentially increasing the stimulus for hypertrophy. Some lean-mass gains may also reflect shifts in intracellular water, so direct-imaging studies generally show a smaller effect than DXA-based lean-mass analyses.
edges.summary: The evidence supports a real but not dramatic hypertrophy edge. Creatine monohydrate tends to increase lean-mass gains during resistance training, though the magnitude is modest and part of the effect may reflect fluid-related changes rather than pure contractile tissue growth.
edges.caveats: Lean-mass outcomes are easier to improve than direct imaging measures of muscle hypertrophy, so studies using DXA or similar methods may slightly overstate practical muscle gain. Effects also vary by age, training status, and protocol duration.

evidence.citation: AshtaryLarkyD et al 2025 J Int Soc Sports Nutr
evidence.notes: Creatine supplementation and resistance training: a comparison between novice and experienced lifters - a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
